sec: Drug-induced nephropathy: NSAIDs and aminoglycosides · p799

items.q: Complete the NSAID pathophysiology flowchart — 1) NSAIDs act on PGE₂/PGI₂  2) Effect on RAAS  3) Final step … A) Stimulation of RAAS  B) ↑K⁺ excretion via aldosterone  C) (–) inhibition
items.exp: NSAID flowchart: NSAIDs (–) PGE₂/PGI₂ → stimulates RAAS → aldosterone → ↑K⁺ excretion. (Book p799)

items.q: A 60-year-old on long-term NSAIDs develops AKI with a urine output of 400 mL/day, FeNa of 0.7% and a K⁺ of 6.4 mEq/L. Which statement matches the book's description?
opts: Oliguria, FeNa <1 and hyperkalemia out of proportion to the renal failure
Polyuria, FeNa <1 and hypokalemia out of proportion to the renal failure
Oliguria, FeNa >2 and hypokalemia with an active urinary sediment
Anuria, FeNa >2 and hyperkalemia with muddy brown epithelial casts
items.exp: NSAID nephropathy clinical features: oliguria, FeNa <1 and hyperkalemia out of proportion. (Book p799)

items.q: All but one of the following are features of NSAID-induced nephropathy. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: NSAID nephropathy: oliguria, FeNa <1 and hyperkalemia out of proportion; FeNa >2% indicates established ATN. (Book p799)

items.q: Complete the aminoglycoside pathophysiology flowchart — 1) Cationic amino groups on the drug  2) Target  3) Intracellular effect … A) Anionic megalin  B) Accumulates in lysosomes after endocytosis causing oxidative stress  C) Binds anionic megalin in the brush border of the PCT
items.exp: Aminoglycoside flowchart: cationic amino groups on the drug bind anionic megalin in the brush border of the PCT; after endocytosis the drug accumulates in lysosomes causing oxidative stress. (Book p799)

items.q: Aminoglycosides are taken up into proximal tubular cells by binding to:
opts: Anionic megalin in the brush border
items.exp: Cationic amino groups on aminoglycosides bind anionic megalin in the brush border of the PCT, are endocytosed, and accumulate in lysosomes causing oxidative stress. (Book p799)

items.q: A patient given gentamicin develops non-oliguric AKI on day 7 of therapy. Which drug-related pattern is described?
opts: Non-oliguric AKI 5–10 days after starting the drug
items.exp: Aminoglycoside clinical features: non-oliguric AKI 5–10 days after the drug — hence renal function must be monitored in this window. (Book p799)

items.q: How is aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity prevented according to the page?
opts: Administer the drug as a single dose, following concentration-dependent killing
Give smaller divided doses three times a day
Combine with a loop diuretic to increase excretion
Give with NSAIDs to reduce tubular inflammation
items.exp: Prevention: administer the aminoglycoside as a single dose, following concentration-dependent killing, rather than by sustained divided dosing. (Book p799)

items.q: Aminoglycoside-induced non-oliguric AKI typically appears how long after the drug?
items.exp: Aminoglycoside clinical features: non-oliguric AKI 5–10 days after the drug. (Book p799)

items.q: All but one of the following are correct about aminoglycoside nephropathy. Which is the odd one out?
opts: It binds megalin in the PCT brush border
It accumulates in lysosomes causing oxidative stress
It appears 5–10 days after the drug
items.exp: Aminoglycosides cause non-oliguric AKI (5–10 days after the drug), with the megalin-lysosome-oxidative stress mechanism. (Book p799)

items.q: Both NSAID and aminoglycoside nephropathy involve active reabsorption pathways in the proximal nephron.
opts: False — only aminoglycosides are taken up by megalin-mediated endocytosis in the PCT
True — NSAIDs are also taken up by megalin-mediated endocytosis in the PCT
False — aminoglycosides act only on the collecting duct, not on the proximal tubule
True, but only when NSAIDs are given together with an aminoglycoside drug
items.exp: Aminoglycosides are endocytosed after binding anionic megalin in the PCT brush border; NSAIDs act by inhibiting PGE₂/PGI₂, stimulating RAAS. (Book p799)
